incident: Refrigeration controllers hijacked at French supermarkets (wave 1)
vulnerability: Internet-exposed Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC, Copeland and Dixell XWEB refrigeration controllers (CERT-FR alert)
scale: 700+ retail sites (Intermarché, Netto, Coopérative U, Carrefour, E.Leclerc, Monoprix); food losses and at least 15 fires

incident: Ahold Delhaize takes IT systems offline after cyberattack
scale: Websites, apps and online shopping offline across most US and European brands; stores stayed open

incident: PHP2Shell: critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws exploited in the wild
vulnerability: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS v4 9.2); fixed in PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12. Separate unpatched CVE-2026-115560 (unusual configs only)
scale: PHP runs most websites; millions of exploit attempts seen; CISA added both to KEV on 26 Oct 2026
ai_detail: Reporting says AI helped find the flaw; no AI use reported in the attacks

incident: Second wave of supermarket refrigeration attacks across Europe
countries: Belgium; Luxembourg; Netherlands; Sweden; Ireland; Finland; Estonia; Germany; Romania; UK
vulnerability: Same controller families; Danfoss says most hacked units were legacy products no longer updated
scale: 100+ stores (incl. Carrefour 15 of 700 Belgian stores, Delhaize, ICA, Coop, an IKEA store); UK meat-storage sites also hit
status: EU called it a deliberate attempt to disrupt the food supply chain

incident: French national blood service cold rooms tampered with via contractor
vulnerability: Remote access to refrigeration contractor Coolworld's cold-storage controls (since disabled)
scale: 3 EFS sites; temperature and defrost thresholds raised; plasma moved or secured, no products lost
Systems holding employee and internal information accessed

incident: AI-directed intrusion campaign using Cairn framework (Unit 42 report)
sector: Semiconductors; defence and policy; civil society
vulnerability: Various; AI tailored the attack vector to each target
scale: 25 operations against at least 19 organisations (Aug–Sep 2026); access or data taken at 10
ai_detail: Customised Cairn AI pentest framework run on Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models; humans chose targets

attribution: Not an attack (Microsoft: no malicious activity)
vulnerability: Exchange Online servers failed health checks
scale: Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot disrupted; ~138,000 Downdetector reports at peak

incident: First fully automated AI attack: 'exploit_agent' hits French websites (Google GTIG)
threat_actor: Russian-speaking operators (not linked to Russian state)
attribution: Assessed by Google; state link not established
vulnerability: Flaws found by AI agents diffing software before and after security patches
scale: Multiple French sites; stolen victim data found on the attackers' server
ai_detail: Multi-agent system found flaws and wrote exploits with no human in the loop (per Google)

incident: Ethiopian Airlines ShebaMiles loyalty programme data breach
scale: Described as 'limited scope'; number affected and data types not disclosed; no evidence financial data was accessed
